en: The *Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Spoken Universal Worthy Dhāraṇī Sūtra*.

[Posthumously honored with the titles: Grand Master of the Household, Peer of the Three Ducal Courts, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sushan with a fief of three thousand households;
invested with purple robes; posthumously granted the rank of Minister of Works and the posthumous title of "Great Mirror."
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, Possessor of Great and Vast Wisdom, by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha.
Together with a great assembly of bhikṣus and ninety-nine koṭis of great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
at that time, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
Rising from his seat within that assembly, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I wish to proclaim the Samantabhadra Dhāraṇī.
World-Honored One, as for this dhāraṇī..."
I received it from the Tathāgata Candraprabhaśrī.
If those belonging to the Bodhisattva Vehicle should hear this dhāraṇī, even for a moment, [they shall attain liberation].
One immediately attains non-retrogression and swiftly serves all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas;
one is able to extinguish all karmic obstructions and obtain peace, happiness, and abundance.
Their bodies attain purity, their verbal karma attains purity, and their minds attain purity.
They penetrate the great ocean of all secrets and are able to fulfill the great ocean of all vows.
I immediately beheld all the Tathāgatas;
by hearing this dhāraṇī,
I realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
They attained the Śūraṅgama-samādhi;
they realized the Ratnamudrā-samādhi, the Arciṣmatī-samādhi, the Sāgaramudrā-samādhi, and the Vyāptākāśa-samādhi.
He realized such samādhi gates as these, numbering as many as the sands of the Ganges;
furthermore, he realized eighty-four thousand dhāraṇī gates, such as the "Opening the Inexhaustible Casket."
By this, one realizes the possession of wisdom and conduct;
one attains such insight and accomplishes the Dharma as it has been heard.
Having heard the Dharma from the various Buddhas, he served and made offerings to them without interruption.
He then said, "I only pray that the World-Honored One will permit me to preach it for the fourfold assembly.
The Buddha said, "I grant you permission to proclaim it."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara entered the samādhi of the Vajra Maṇḍala and spoke this dhāraṇī:
Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya.
Ānanda, he cries out: "Kha! Gaiveyaka! Kha! Gaiveyaka!
Kha! Aveyakṣu! Kha! Kha! Trākṣa! Kha! Kharaṇa! Kha! Erhava! Kha! Kāya! Kha! Ma!"
Nakha-vaiśāra-khavaive-makhavai-śūraṃ-khavai-nimitta-khavai-praṇidhāna-khavai-samādhi-khavai-prāmodya-khavai-ṛddhi-khavai-sara sara sara sarva-buddha.
ĀṬ ḌĪ ṬE VARA VARA DHARMA ṬE KARA KARA KARA SAṄGHA ṬE NAMA ĀRYA VAJRACCHEDIŚVARĀYA BODHISATTVA.
Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya nāmodbhūtanāmadheye adhiṣṭhitu māṃ āyur.
Oṃ lañjanadundataye ta su-ra-bhi su-ra-bhi mu-ni mu-ni ma-hā-mu-ni mati mati mahā-mati namo 'rya-avalokiteśvarāya bodhi...
*Sattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya sidhyantu samantabhadradhāraṇī svāhā.* At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
When this dhāraṇī was being spoken,
ninety-two koṭis of bodhisattvas realized the śūraṅgama-samādhi.
Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges have realized the subtle and wondrous dhāraṇī-samādhi;
I shall now proclaim the merits of this dhāraṇī.
Every morning,
recite this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times for a full twenty-one days.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will then manifest his body,
and all the aspirations one seeks shall be fully satisfied.
If a person is imprisoned or bound in shackles and chains...
If one recites and maintains this for seven days, one will immediately attain liberation.
If a person suffers from malaria,
by reciting it beside the left ear of the patient, the illness will be cured.
If a person suffers from diseases caused by wind or afflictions by malevolent spirits,
one should empower clarified butter mixed with oil twenty-one times;
if they are made to ingest it, they will immediately be cured.
If one suffers from toothache,
consecrate a tooth-stick twenty-one times;
by chewing it, the pain will be cured.
If one suffers from earache,
take cotton-seed oil and place it in a vessel of refined copper; empower it seven times with mantras.
If one drips [the medicine] into the ear, it is immediately cured.
If one suffers from headaches or abdominal pain,
by consecrating the hand and stroking [the afflicted area], it is immediately cured.
If one suffers from demonic possession,
tie a mantra-empowered cord and consecrate it one hundred and eight times;
if it is worn, one will be healed immediately.
If one is possessed by a ḍākinī,
empower oil seven times and rub it onto the joints and limbs; one will immediately be healed.
If one suffers from any illness, by consecrating either the hand or a willow branch and stroking the afflicted area, one is immediately healed.
As with all the aforementioned methods, no laborious practice is required; efficacy follows immediately upon recitation.
If one wishes to seek a vision of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
to realize the gates of dhāraṇī and samādhi,
or to attain supernatural powers, invisibility, and the ointment of añjana;
Regarding the accomplishment of the medicinal substance realgar:
the practitioner, before a stūpa containing relics or an image of the Buddha,
should smear a maṇḍala and suspend silk banners and canopies.
Scatter various kinds of flowers and burn sandalwood, aloeswood, and frankincense;
light one hundred lamps for a vast offering.
The practitioner of recitation shall bathe and purify themselves.
Wearing clean garments and maintaining pure conduct,
one should then recite this dhāraṇī for binding the boundaries of the cardinal directions, which says:

*Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo 'ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya. Tadyathā: ciri maṃdame, mili maṃda me, ciri mili maṃda me, sima maṃda me, sima maṃdame, kṣiñjati na ti krama tu svāhā.* With this *dhāraṇī*, empower water twenty-one times.
By sprinkling [water] throughout the ten directions within the site of enlightenment (maṇḍala), one immediately establishes the boundary (sīmābandha).
I shall now recite the dhāraṇī for invitation;
the practitioner of the mantra-path (mantrayānin), having first recited this dhāraṇī, performs the invitation.
Then, perform the recitation.
The *dhāraṇī* is as follows:

*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | ciri ciri miri miri ciriḍe | ehi bhagavan āryāvalokiteśvara svāhā.* This *dhāraṇī* is my heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*).
By reciting the mantra, the invocation is immediately accomplished.
The practitioner begins on the eighth day of the waxing moon and continues until the fifteenth day.
Recite one hundred and eight times during each of the three periods of the day.
Bathe at these three times and change your clothes at these three times.
On the fifteenth day, perform an extensive offering and limitless recitation.
At midnight on that day, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara came to the site of practice,
manifesting a golden-hued body, with marks and signs of excellence,
dignified and majestic, emitting hundreds of thousands of rays of light.
The reciter should not feel fear, but should instead give rise to a mind of courageous strength.
Upon merely seeing Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
one immediately attains the stages of realization and realizes dhāraṇī-samādhi.
He immediately beheld Akṣobhya Tathāgata in the east, Ratnākara Tathāgata in the south, Amitāyus Tathāgata in the west, and Devadundubhisvararāja Tathāgata in the north.
He beheld the four Tathāgatas and the vast majesty of the bodies of the infinite Tathāgatas of the ten directions, who,
sustained by the power of the great compassionate vows of all Buddhas,
abide long in the world.
Upon passing away from this life, one shall be reborn in the pure and wondrous Buddha-field,
where in all places one shall make offerings to and serve all the Tathāgatas.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra,
the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, along with the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, [all rejoiced].
All were greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The *Universal Worthy Dhāraṇī Sūtra* Spoken by Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Namaḥ samantabhadraya | Oṃ maṇi padme hūṃ | Tadyathā | Oṃ gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā.
